rationale.headline: Platform-sized fit: 6 closed adjacent deals in band, 5 deals in 3 years, but no Healthcare Services history.
rationale.acquirer_overview: Hellman & Friedman is a financial sponsor with 15 deals in 2015-2024, 5 in the last 3 years, most in Physician Groups (3) and Home Health/Hospice (3). Its size sweet spot is $88.6-437.2M (IQR), it most often buys from Private sellers (7 of 15), and its most common financing is Leveraged and Mixed (4 each of 15). Its history shows a spread across provider and services niches rather than one sector, with 3 SPAC Merger labels in the mix.
rationale.strategic_fit_thesis: The size role is platform, inside its interquartile range $88.6-437.2M, so Project Atlas at $200M would be a standalone platform rather than an add-on. Nearest adjacent evidence is physician and billing services: [MA-2024-0002] at $298.6M, 5 bidders, and [MA-2023-0379] at $446.8M in Revenue Cycle with a 24.2% margin, close to Atlas's 21.5%. Both are labelled Bolt-on Acquisition, a noisy label we treat only as a data point. Versus closest competitor Welsh Carson, H&F has fewer deals (15 vs 23) and fewer in the target sector (0 vs 1), and a similar median size ($187.3M vs $172.3M). Deployment pace is lower, 5 deals in the last 3 years vs 8. H&F's median size sits close to Atlas's $200M, but it has less pace and no sector history.

precedent_activity.why_relevant: Most recent and highest-relevance deal: $298.6M Physician Groups, Southeast, 13.3x EV/EBITDA, leveraged, usable as a control comp.
Revenue Cycle deal at $446.8M and 18.4x with a 24.2% margin, the closest margin match to Atlas; Private seller, 5 bidders.
Dental LBO at $427.6M, 13.0x, Private seller with stock financing and 2 bidders; shows a private-seller control deal in a services niche.

rationale.valuation_context: On how it pays, H&F's closed adjacent control deals show a median 15.8x EV/EBITDA (n=6, interquartile 13.8x-16.3x), which is above its Financial Sponsor peers at 13.5x, a gap of 2.3 turns. Its precedents span 13.0x [MA-2020-0286] to 18.4x [MA-2023-0379], so a higher-margin target like Atlas could clear at the upper part of its own range. The 3 most relevant multiples are usable as control comps. The SPAC Merger [MA-2022-0007] is excluded as a comp.

risk_flags.detail: Three withdrawn deals: [MA-2015-0250] at $199.3M, [MA-2020-0447] at $187.3M and [MA-2022-0056] at $27.2M. The first two are almost exactly Atlas's size, so H&F has walked away from or lost deals at this scale.
Zero deals in Healthcare Services, the target sector, and only 2 relevant closed deals out of 15, so the sector-specific evidence is thin.
33.3% of deals are leveraged or seller-financed, and 3 deals are stock-financed. A $200M platform sits well below its largest closed deal of $994.1M, so size is not the constraint.
Its precedents show up to 5 bidders [MA-2024-0002][MA-2023-0379] against an average of 2.8, so a contested process could test its above-peer pricing.

conviction.rationale: Suggested Medium stands. Supports: 6 closed adjacent-sector deals in the size band, 2 in the last 3 years, and a platform size role. Against: 0 Healthcare Services deals and 3 withdrawn deals.
